doc.title: Hide Tanaka interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 3, 2014

title: Playing the bass at the American Embassy to get the green card
summary: He borrowed a bass, got it past embassy security, and played Saints and You Are My Sunshine with an officer on guitar, winning his green card.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: And I asked so many people, and so many American people were kind of laughing. They know what happens even inside the embassy, the American Embassy people were kind of laughing. And some guy just came out and he didn’t even see me but he just “don’t give up, don’t give up. Anyway, you can do it yourself, just try it.” Anyway I came back to my hotel and I started calling the people and “can you borrow me the bass, just one day?” “No way.” And the next day I went back to the American Embassy with a bass. But even security did not say yes. They said “what, this is the American Embassy. What are you doing with this big thing?” But I still remember the name of Kim. And my officer, she said I have to prove my occupation. This is just the only way I am able to prove. So the security guy went inside of the building and called the police in Japanese and the police came back and said “oh I really don’t know how the Americans are thinking.” Anyway “I’m sorry, sir, you can come in with that.” And I got inside and I had an interview. And I brought the bass with the glass window.

And he said, “okay, show me.” And the funny thing, inside, some officer brought a guitar. And she said “we have a musician too. So you must play with our musician.” Because he was an officer you know. So anyway he started tuning. Very out of tune. And “hey wait, I’m with you tuning up. I cannot play with you.” And he started playing, kind of red faced. “Oh really?”
Oh you mean he’s got the toot-toot, the tuning whistle.
You’re lucky they didn’t boot you out of the country.

And after that, I said “I want to play ‘Saints Go Marching In’ key of D.” And also he sung. And there’s a window. He’s inside. I’m outside. And everybody’s waiting, what the hell is going on. And the Navy’s people come in and they started clapping. Oh man that sounds good. And I finished. And he said “can we play one more? ‘You Are My Sunshine.’ Also key of D.” © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -7-

And he sang. And after that my officer came and said “we’ll have a party later tonight.” It’s a kind of joke. I said yes but I’m very expensive. And he was laughing. Then, after that, he gave me the green card.
